sections.heading: Jake White emerges as favourite to take over as Fiji head coach
sections.body: Former World Cup-winning coach Jake White has emerged as the leading candidate to fill the vacant Fiji head coach role. According to reports in South Africa, the 2007 Springboks mastermind is considered the frontrunner from a 31-man shortlist that includes Warren Gatland. White, who last coached at international level nearly two decades ago, recently expressed his desire for a return, stating, “I still think I have unfinished business at the Test level.” The Fiji Rugby Union is set to name its decision in the coming days.

lead.why: Jake White has emerged as the favourite on the Fiji Rugby Union's head coach shortlist.

sections.heading: Jake White emerges as early favourite to become new Fiji coach

The new coach takes the Flying Fijians into November's Nations Championship.

sections.heading: Owen Doyle blasts Hooper and Hansen's 'totally out of order' Piardi remarks
sections.body: Former Test referee and ex-IRFU director of referees Owen Doyle has hit out at Michael Hooper and Steve Hansen for their criticism of Andrea Piardi, after the Italian took charge of Australia's 42-38 win over South Africa in Perth. Piardi issued four yellow cards — one leading to a ban for Hunter Paisami — and had to referee without a working TMO link. Hooper suggested World Rugby stop sending Piardi to Wallabies matches; Doyle called that line of attack unwarranted, insisting only one card was wrongly given and that wasn't the referee's fault.

lead.why: Freshest, highest-scoring story with a genuine Irish voice (Owen Doyle) weighing into a live officiating row, and the only candidate not already covered or a repeat of recent editions.

sections.heading: Argentina leads four-nation proposal to host 2035 Rugby World Cup
sections.body: The Argentine Rugby Union has officially launched a joint bid alongside Uruguay, Brazil and Chile to host the 2035 Rugby World Cup. The proposal features iconic stadiums across the region, including the Monumental and José Amalfitani in Buenos Aires, alongside Brazil’s Maracanã. Félix Páez Molina stated the candidacy represents a "very important step" for the sport. World Rugby expects to announce the host in November 2027, with the potential for the tournament to reach South America for the first time.

lead.why: Argentina is spearheading a major multi-nation bid to host the 2035 Rugby World Cup.

sections.heading: Argentina formalises 2035 tournament hosting proposal alongside three South American neighbours
sections.body: Argentina has officially submitted the required technical information to World Rugby to formalise its joint 2035 Rugby World Cup bid alongside Uruguay, Chile and Brazil. Félix Páez Molina, President of the Argentine Rugby Union, described the candidacy as a significant step for the region, noting that the four-nation project aims to showcase South American passion for the sport. If successful, the tournament would see matches staged at iconic venues including the Maracanã in Brazil and the Estadio Monumental in Buenos Aires.

lead.why: The brief requires a new story and this candidate provides the most recent development on the joint 2035 World Cup bid.

sections.heading: Argentina's 2035 World Cup bid set to challenge Europe's return hopes
sections.body: Argentina's joint South American bid for the 2035 Rugby World Cup, fronted alongside Uruguay, Chile and Brazil, is shaping up as a direct challenge to World Rugby's apparent preference for a European host, according to Planet Rugby. Japan, Spain and Italy remain in contention, while a Saudi-backed Gulf bid has reportedly collapsed and South Africa are said to be weighing a return bid of their own, though financial constraints may rule it out. World Rugby names its preferred host in May 2027, with the Council deciding that November.

lead.why: Adds the genuinely new element today — the rival bids and World Rugby's apparent European lean — rather than re-running yesterday's announcement.

sections.heading: Justin Marshall slams Hunter Paisami's Bledisloe Cup suspension as 'absolute joke'

Ex-Wallaby Jeremy Paul and Kieran Read agreed, with Paul revealing Len Ikitau's ankle knock from the Springboks win is likely only bone bruising — easing fears over Les Kiss's midfield ahead of Saturday's opener at Eden Park.

sections.heading: Wallabies scrum-half Ryan Lonergan credits Japanese player for passing technique
sections.body: Australia’s Ryan Lonergan has revealed that a specialist grip tape technique, learned from Japanese half-back Kaito Shigeno during their time with the Barbarians in 2023, has become essential to his game. Lonergan explained that the tape helps him maintain consistent passing in wet or sweaty conditions, noting that he now regularly stocks up on the equipment whenever he visits Japan. The Wallabies No. 9 has successfully integrated this Japanese-inspired tactic into his international performances as he prepares for his 13th Test.

sections.heading: Wallabies' Ryan Lonergan Credits Japanese Half-Back Kaito Shigeno For Grip Tape
sections.body: Wallabies scrum-half Ryan Lonergan says the finger-taping habit that has powered his in-form season came from Kaito Shigeno, the Japanese half-back he played alongside for the Barbarians in 2023. Lonergan, who kicked 17 points in Australia's 42-38 win over South Africa, revealed Shigeno gave him a box of specialist grip tape he still uses in matches — though never at training. "I found it's a way for me to be able to pass consistently in the game," he said ahead of Saturday's clash with Cam Roigard's All Blacks at Eden Park.

sections.heading: South Africa enters contention as potential 2035 Rugby World Cup host
sections.body: South Africa has emerged as a dark horse contender to host the 2035 Rugby World Cup as World Rugby advances its bidding process. While the governing body has signalled a preference for returning the tournament to Europe, site visits and feasibility assessments are set to continue through early next year. World Rugby is considering both single-country proposals and multi-territory consortiums, with a final decision on the preferred host expected by May 2027 before the formal appointment in November 2027.

lead.why: It addresses South Africa's emerging position as a contender for a major future hosting opportunity.
